content: The Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences (PGSS) is a prestigious five-week summer program designed for gifted high school students in Pennsylvania. It is part of the Pennsylvania Governor's Schools of Excellence and has been hosted by Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh since its establishment in 1982. The program is currently directed by Dr. Barry Luokkala. Eligible participants must be Pennsylvania high school students transitioning between their junior and senior years, and they are required to reside in the dormitories for the entire duration of the program. Admission is highly competitive, with approximately 500 applicants vying for 100 available spots (recently increased from 90). The primary goal of PGSS is to foster a passion for science rather than to provide advanced knowledge in a specific field. The curriculum includes five core courses in Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics, and Physics, along with a variety of elective courses. Students are also required to engage in a laboratory course and participate in a research-oriented team project. The program emphasizes collaboration over competition, encouraging students to work together academically and socially. The core courses are taught by instructors who are not restricted to specific subfields, allowing for variation in course content from year to year. Common topics include HIV/AIDS Biotechnology in Biology, Organic Chemistry in Chemistry, Discrete Mathematics in Mathematics, and Modern Physics—often focusing on Special Relativity—in Physics. The Computer Science course typically covers fundamental programming concepts and offers independent study opportunities for experienced students. Given the diverse academic backgrounds of participants, peer support is a common and encouraged practice to manage the workload. Core courses are generally 50 minutes long and held four days a week, with four courses scheduled daily from Monday to Friday. Students may drop one core course after two weeks if they are enrolled in at least one elective and have completed all outstanding assignments for the dropped course. Laboratory courses are offered in all subjects except Mathematics, with some interdisciplinary options available. These labs usually meet twice a week for three hours. Depending on the subject, students may be required to align their laboratory course with their team project area. Elective courses, which are among the most variable components of the program, typically run for one hour twice a week. Students are not allowed to take more than three electives in addition to all core courses without special permission from the program director. Certain electives, such as Astrophysics and various Mathematics topics, are consistently offered each year, though their content may change. Participation in a team project is mandatory for all PGSS students. These projects generally align with the core course subjects and culminate in a final scientific research paper. The results are presented during the program's final week, known as Team Project Week, during which no classes are held to allow students to focus on their research and presentations. The final papers are compiled into the PGSS Journal. Homework assignments are a significant component of the program, with students typically required to submit one assignment per week for each core course, as well as any homework for their electives. The program aims to replicate the collaborative nature of the modern scientific community by encouraging students to work together on assignments. Homework problems are intentionally designed to be time-intensive and challenging, promoting teamwork and a cooperative learning environment. Additionally, students are not ranked among their peers, eliminating competitive pressures and fostering a sense of community.
